implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the pattern into property delegation: `val real: Image by lazy { Image.load(path) }` runs the initializer on the first get() and returns the remembered result from then on, with SYNCHRONIZED (the default) making the initialization single-flight, PUBLICATION letting threads race while keeping one winner, and NONE dropping synchronization entirely. The stdlib documents that a throwing initializer is not cached - the next access retries - and that SYNCHRONIZED may synchronize on the delegate itself, so external code must not lock it. The classic stand-in class is only needed when the proxy must satisfy a multi-method interface, forward identity, or swap the real subject at runtime.
pitfalls: Do not synchronize on the Lazy instance from outside; the stdlib warns that SYNCHRONIZED may use the delegate as its lock and external locking can deadlock.
NONE is unspecified under concurrency and PUBLICATION may run the initializer several times and discard the losers, so both are only safe when construction is idempotent or genuinely single-threaded.
A `by lazy` in a companion object is initialized once per class, not once per instance - per-instance deferral requires the delegate to be an instance property.
